We just shipped JSEF v1.4.0-benchmark 🚀
A Spring Boot 3.x Java vuln-mining benchmark, now +85 samples (503→588 checkpoints), all passing dual-source validation.
Mapped to OWASP BenchmarkJava, java-sec-code, JavaSecLab, micro_service_seclab, WebGoat & CodeQL.
SSRF, JWT, IDOR,

1/ What's JSEF? A Spring Boot 3.x security-teaching framework + a benchmark for evaluating SAST tools & LLM vuln-finding. Every sample carries a machine-readable // [CHECKPOINT] + CSV pair with a hard gate (validate exits 0 or it's not
  done).

2/ This release closes gaps vs 5 top Java vuln benchmarks + CodeQL's Java query suite. New categories:
  • SSRF, JWT, open-redirect, CRLF
  • weak randomness/crypto, IDOR, missing authz, race conditions
  • Log4j2 JNDI, Shiro, Fastjson, XStream/Jackson/SnakeYAML

3/ Bonus for SAST eval: 13 "looks-vuln-but-safe" FP-trap samples (generic numeric SQL, MyBatis #{}, allowlist paths, htmlEscape…) so tools are scored on false positives too — true TN/FP, not just recall.
4/ Safety-first: component CVE samples only show the dangerous trigger + safe config. No exploit payloads, no live JNDI/gadget chains. Every vuln ships with a sec fix counterpart.

5/ All 588 checkpoints pass validate_checkpoints.py (0 orphans / duplicates / drift). Try it: python3 benchmark/scripts/scorecard.py
  Full notes 👉 https://t.co/lBeV7mWnRE
